belize/xunantunich.name: Xunantunich Maya site
belize/xunantunich.description: A hilltop Maya city near San Ignacio, reached by a hand-cranked ferry, with a climbable pyramid.
belize/xunantunich.details: Xunantunich was a major Maya centre, and El Castillo pyramid rises about 40 metres, with a view into Guatemala. The way in includes a small hand-cranked ferry across the Mopan River. Go in the morning, because it gets hot, and bring water. It is about fifteen minutes from San Ignacio.

belize/atm-cave.name: Actun Tunichil Muknal (ATM) cave
belize/atm-cave.description: A guided wade-and-swim cave expedition to a chamber of Maya sacrificial remains.
belize/atm-cave.details: ATM involves a jungle hike, wading through the river and swimming into the cave, then climbing to a chamber of ceremonial pottery and skeletons, including the crystal maiden. Only licensed guides may take groups, and cameras are no longer allowed inside. Participants must be reasonably fit and comfortable in water. Book in advance, as numbers are limited.

belize/caracol.name: Caracol Maya site
belize/caracol.description: The largest Maya site in Belize, deep in the Chiquibul forest, with a pyramid that is the tallest man-made structure in the country.
belize/caracol.details: Caracol was once larger than present-day Belize City, and Caana is a great temple complex rising above the canopy. The drive from San Ignacio takes two hours on rough roads, often with a stop at Rio On pools and Rio Frio cave. Go with a guide, because road conditions vary with rain.

belize/cave-tubing.name: Cave tubing
belize/cave-tubing.description: A float through limestone caves on an inner tube, with a jungle walk to reach the river.
belize/cave-tubing.details: Cave tubing is a relaxed activity at Nohoch Che'en or Caves Branch, with a short jungle trail carrying the tubes. Guides give headlamps and life jackets. It is wet and suits families and those who prefer an easier option than ATM. Water levels can change after rain.

belize/caye-caulker-snorkel.name: Hol Chan and Shark Ray Alley snorkelling
belize/caye-caulker-snorkel.description: A boat snorkel trip to a marine reserve and a spot where nurse sharks and stingrays gather.
belize/caye-caulker-snorkel.details: The Hol Chan Marine Reserve protects coral and fish at a gap in the barrier reef, and Shark Ray Alley is where nurse sharks and southern stingrays swim around the boat. Trips from Caye Caulker last a half day. The animals are used to people, but follow the guide advice and keep your distance.

belize/great-blue-hole.name: Great Blue Hole
belize/great-blue-hole.description: A huge marine sinkhole in the middle of the Lighthouse Reef atoll, seen by air or on a dive.
belize/great-blue-hole.details: The Great Blue Hole is over 300 metres wide and about 125 metres deep. Most visitors see it from the air on a short scenic flight from Belize City or Caye Caulker, as boat trips are long and snorkelling is limited. Certified divers can descend to see stalactites. Flights depend on weather.

belize/caye-caulker-island.name: Caye Caulker island life
belize/caye-caulker-island.description: A small car-free island with sandy lanes, a Split for swimming and relaxed bars.
belize/caye-caulker-island.details: Caye Caulker has a Go Slow motto, with golf-cart and bike travel, and a channel called The Split where people swim and sunbathe. Cafes serve lobster in season, from July to February for lobster. Sunsets from the western side are a good evening activity.

belize/cockscomb.name: Cockscomb Basin Wildlife Sanctuary
belize/cockscomb.description: A jaguar reserve with jungle walks, waterfalls and river tubing.
belize/cockscomb.details: The reserve was created to protect jaguars, and the cats are rarely seen, though other wildlife and birds are common. Trails lead to waterfalls and viewing towers. Tubing on the South Stann Creek is a gentle option. Bring insect repellent and water.

belize/placencia.name: Placencia village and beach
belize/placencia.description: A narrow peninsula with a long sandy beach, a sidewalk village and seafood cafes.
belize/placencia.details: Placencia has some of the best beaches in mainland Belize, and the main village is built around a sidewalk said to be the narrowest street in the world. Boats leave for the cays and the reef, and the area is a base for manatee and whale shark tours in season. It is calmer than the northern cayes.

belize/laughing-bird-caye.name: Laughing Bird Caye and the southern reef
belize/laughing-bird-caye.description: A tiny island in a marine park with calm snorkelling and diving.
belize/laughing-bird-caye.details: Laughing Bird Caye is a national park and part of the barrier reef system, reached by boat from Placencia. The snorkelling is easy and the water clear in the dry season. Whale sharks gather in the area in spring around the full moon, from March to June.

belize/rio-frio-pine-ridge.name: Mountain Pine Ridge and Big Rock Falls
belize/rio-frio-pine-ridge.description: A cool pine highland with waterfalls, caves and swimming holes south of San Ignacio.
belize/rio-frio-pine-ridge.details: The Mountain Pine Ridge reserve has pine forest, rivers and waterfalls such as Big Rock Falls and the Rio On pools, plus the Rio Frio cave. A guide can combine them with Caracol. Roads are unpaved and can be slippery after rain.

belize/blue-hole-national-park.name: Blue Hole National Park and St Herman's Cave
belize/blue-hole-national-park.description: An inland blue hole swimming spot reached by a short walk along the Hummingbird Highway.
belize/blue-hole-national-park.details: The inland Blue Hole is a cenote with a cool turquoise pool, a short walk from the car park. It is a pleasant stop between San Ignacio and Placencia. St Herman's cave is nearby and can be explored with a headlamp. It is a different place from the offshore Great Blue Hole.

belize.name: Belize
belize.description: A small Caribbean-facing country of Maya ruins, caves, jungle and a barrier reef.

belize/cayo.name: Cayo
belize/cayo.description: The western jungle district of caves, waterfalls and Maya sites.

belize/san-ignacio.name: San Ignacio
belize/san-ignacio.description: A lively market town and base for caves, Maya sites and river trips.

belize/stann-creek.name: Stann Creek
belize/stann-creek.description: The southern coastal district of Placencia, Hopkins and Cockscomb Basin.

belize/placencia.name: Placencia
belize/placencia.description: A beach peninsula and village on the Caribbean coast.

belize/caye-caulker.name: Caye Caulker
belize/caye-caulker.description: A car-free island on the barrier reef, known for snorkelling and relaxed living.
